extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: MMStar is a premier, vision-critical multi-modal benchmark that includes 1,500 challenging samples, each rigorously validated by humans. It is structured to test 6 fundamental capabilities and 18 specific dimensions, aiming to evaluate the multi-modal capacities of LVLMs with a carefully balanced and purified selection of samples.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Samples were first roughly selected from existing benchmarks using an automated pipeline with LLM inspectors, then underwent strict manual review by three experts. The automated pipeline used 8 LLMs (2 closed-source and 6 open-source) to filter samples, retaining only those with 2 or fewer correct answers from the LLM inspectors. Manual review ensured visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and requirement of advanced multi-modal capabilities. Finally, 1,500 high-quality samples were curated from 11,607 coarsely filtered samples.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consisted of 22,401 samples from six existing benchmarks: two benchmarks focused on natural images and four centered on scientific and technical knowledge. These samples were sourced from existing multi-modal evaluation benchmarks.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts conducted manual review to ensure: 1) each sample's answer should be based on understanding of visual content; 2) selected samples should cover comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; 3) most samples should require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution. Experts reviewed samples split into four difficulty categories (easy, moderate, hard, tough) based on LVLM hit counts, and manually curated 1,500 high-quality samples considering both diversity of capability dimensions and difficulty levels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Samples were validated to meet three fundamental criteria: 1) Visual dependency - samples can only be correctly answered based on understanding visual content; 2) Minimal data leakage - samples minimize risk of unintentional inclusion in LLMs' training corpus; 3) Requiring advanced multi-modal capabilities for resolution. Automated pipeline used 8 LLMs as inspectors, retaining only samples with 2 or fewer hits (75% of LLM inspectors fail to provide correct answer).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automated pipeline using 8 LLMs as inspectors for initial filtering: 2 closed-source LLMs (GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro) and 6 open-source LLMs (LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, and others sizing 20B or larger). Open-source LLMs applied with 2-shot in-context inference strategy. 16 leading LVLMs (GPT4V, GeminiPro-Vision, LLaVA series) used to gauge sample difficulty and split into four levels.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark identifies that existing multi-modal evaluation datasets contain samples where visual content is unnecessary - answers can be inferred from questions/options alone or from world knowledge embedded in LLMs. For example, GeminiPro achieves 42.9% on MMMU without visual input, and over 50% of ScienceQA questions can be solved by most LLMs directly without images.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset acknowledges two primary limitations in existing benchmarks: (1) many samples lack visual dependency where answers can be inferred without images, and (2) unintentional data leakage exists in LLM and LVLM training, where models can answer visual-necessary questions without visual content due to memorization from training data. These issues lead to misjudgments of actual multi-modal performance gains.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: MMStar is designed as an evaluation benchmark to assess the multi-modal capabilities of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs). It comprises 1,500 samples for testing 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, with strict manual review to ensure visual dependency and minimal data leakage. The benchmark is intended to evaluate actual multi-modal performance gains rather than text-only capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set in the future and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM's and LVLM's training corpora.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Samples were filtered and balanced across difficulty levels and capability dimensions. The dataset was split into four difficulty categories (easy: 12-16 hits, moderate: 8-11 hits, hard: 4-7 hits, tough: 0-3 hits) based on LVLM hit counts. Final selection ensured balanced distribution with 250 samples per core capability across 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated pipeline filtered samples using LLM inspectors (2 closed-source and 6 open-source LLMs sized 20B or larger with 2-shot in-context inference). Only samples with 2 or fewer hits (indicating ~75% of LLM inspectors failed) were retained, reducing the pool from 22,401 to 11,607 samples. This was followed by manual review by three experts to ensure visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and requirement of advanced multi-modal capabilities.
